base: NOAUTH  tfc \[optional\]: account, no local client to detect · not authenticated \(\$TFC_API_TOKEN rejected\) -> STEP-tfc
head: NOCHECK tfc \[optional\]: account, no local client to detect · authentication not checked \(service unreachable\) -> STEP-tfc
replace: <the tfc line when the proxy refuses a plain-http target>
why: QA B2 on PR #538: both sides now honour http_proxy and HTTP_PROXY (urllib's ProxyHandler; the Node GET's worker starts with --use-env-proxy), and with no_proxy naming the host both go direct and agree (step 3, compared). The residual is how a plain-http target reaches the proxy: urllib sent it an absolute-form GET and read the refusing proxy's own 502 as the service's answer (NOAUTH, token rejected); fetch opens a CONNECT tunnel, the refusal fails the request, and the GET reads status 0 (NOCHECK). Only the loopback test override is plain http; the real services are https, which both reach through CONNECT. Neither side reads OK.

head: \{"proxy":"CONNECT <SERVICE-HOST>"\}
why: The other half of the entry above, in the stand-in proxy's own log: the base sent it an absolute-form GET of the service URL, the head a CONNECT to the service's host and port. Both reached the proxy, which is what parity with urllib's ProxyHandler required; the request form is fetch's.

base: OK      beta \[optional\]: present \(jq\)\nOK      gamma \[required\]: present \(jq 1\.7\.1\)\nPREREQ  0 required
head: ABSENT  beta \[optional\]: missing \(jq not found\) -> STEP-beta\nMISSING gamma \[required\]: missing \(jq not found\) -> STEP-gamma\nPREREQ  1 required
replace: <a tool found only through a relative PATH entry>
why: QA B2 on PR #538: shutil.which searched a relative PATH entry (here rel, from the current directory) and found rel/jq; src/lib/onpath.js searches absolute entries only, as every moved Node command does, so a current directory cannot decide which program runs. A tool found only through a relative or empty entry therefore reads missing: a false red (exit 1), never a false OK. docs/prerequisites.md says so.

head: "code": 1
replace: "code": <0 with the relative entry searched, 1 without>
why: The exit code of the entry above: the required gamma item is found through the relative entry on the base (exit 0) and missing on the head (exit 1).

head: present \(git 2\.3\.4\)
replace: present (git <the version a probe child reports>)
why: A narrowing (lens F1 on PR #538): prerequisites.py ran every probe child (git, gh, terraform, each --version) with the caller's whole environment, so SONAR_TOKEN and TFC_API_TOKEN reached them. The Node check removes every variable a declaration item names as its auth.env before it starts a probe; the token is read only by this process, for its own GET. The case's git shim reports 9.9.9 when it can see a token and 2.3.4 when it cannot, so the base shows the token passed on and the head shows it withheld. test/check/prerequisites.test.js holds the same property with logging shims.

replace: <a project AGENTS.md that is not UTF-8: reported, not a traceback>
why: merge_authority.check_project read the project's AGENTS.md with read_text(encoding='utf-8') and caught only OSError, so a brief that is not UTF-8 raised UnicodeDecodeError (a ValueError) out of mhw check: a Python traceback on stderr and exit 1, with no PROJECT line. The Node check catches the decode error and reports it as a finding on stdout (next entry). The exit code is 1 on both sides and is compared.

head: PROJECT merge authority: FAIL the AGENTS\.md at <TMP>/work/p is not readable UTF-8; the project brief must declare its merge-authority block\n$
replace: <the PROJECT line for an AGENTS.md that is not UTF-8>
why: The other half of the entry above: where workstation.py stopped with a traceback, the Node check prints one PROJECT FAIL line naming the brief as not readable UTF-8, after the prerequisites section, in the place every other project finding is printed. It is a finding (exit 1), not a fail-closed exit 2, because the installed contract was read and only the project's own file is at fault, as a missing AGENTS.md already was.
